Everything here needs the **Manage events** permission (officers have it by default). Every editor screen is private to you.

## Creating an event

Run `/event-create` with a **title**, a **date** (`YYYY-MM-DD`) and a **time** (`HH:MM`, 24-hour). Times are your server's timezone; add `UTC` after the time to give it in UTC. The editor opens straight away, with four tabs:

- **Core Info**: title, description, the event type, and a banner (an image link, or one from your banner library). Your server's own event types are under **🏷️ Our event types**; make them in `/guild-settings show` → **Features & limits** → **🏷️ Event types** (a name, an emoji and a line of description).
- **Schedule**: the channel it posts in, the date and time, how long it lasts, and whether it repeats.
- **Signups**: whether members can sign up, the answer buttons, limits, when signups close, and whether attendance is recorded.
- **Notifications**: a reminder before the start, a role to ping, how early each week's event is posted, and a temporary role for those signed up.

Changes collect under **Pending changes** at the bottom. **💾 Save** keeps them; **📢 Post to channel** saves and puts the event up for members. The editor closes itself after about half an hour of no use; `/event-list` reopens it.

## Sign-up options

On the **Signups** tab:

- **Max attendees** limits the first answer (Will Attend). Leave it blank for no limit.
- **Signups close** stops new answers at a set time.
- **Response labels** renames the three buttons, one per line. Add a number after a colon to give one its own limit, for example `Subs:10`.
- **Multi-Response** lets members pick more than one answer.
- **Signup role** limits who can sign up to one role.
- **Record attendance** decides whether the event gets an attendance step when it starts. It needs signups on.

## Templates

A template is a ready-made event: its type, title and description, length, attendee limit, role slots, reminder and timing, answers, and whether it repeats -- everything except the date, time and channel. Make them under **📋 Event templates** on the **Features & limits** tab of `/guild-settings show`: **➕ New template**, then fill in each part (**Name & type**, **Timing**, **Sign-ups**, **Extras** for a banner and roles, and, for a game such as DC Dark Legion, its own settings like the Team Post time). Your game may come with some built in.

Then **New event** on the officer panel asks which game (only if your server has two or more), then which template (or **Start blank**), then the title, date and time. The event opens in the editor with the template's settings, ready to adjust and post. `/event-create` takes a **template** too. The Free plan holds 3 templates of your own.

## Role slots

For a raid or anything with set roles, open the **Sign-ups** tab and press **Edit** beside **Role slots**. The form starts with your game's usual set for that kind of event when Alagos knows one, otherwise **Tank 2 / Healer 4 / DPS 14** -- except in games without classes, such as DC Dark Legion, where it starts empty; change it to your own, one role a line, like `🛡️ Tank: 2` or `Shotcaller: 1`. **Start from** in the same form replaces the roles with one of the ready-made sets. Leave the box empty to switch role slots off.

With role slots, the post has a button per role (or one **Sign up** button with a menu, past five roles) instead of Will Attend; Tentative and Won't Attend stay. When a role is full, the next people go on its **bench** in the order they signed up, and move up by themselves when a place frees. Members can name a second choice ("Tank, or DPS if Tank is full") and, if they have more than one character in the game, which one is coming.

**👥 Roles** on the post shows each role and its bench, and lets officers move someone into a role, onto the bench, or back to sign-up order. Attendance is pre-filled with the people in slots, not the bench.

## A temporary role for those signed up

On the **Notifications** tab, **Temporary role** gives a role to everyone signed up for the event and takes it away afterwards, so you can ping that night's roster or open a voice or text channel just to them. Pick an existing role (make one in Discord first, for example "Raid tonight").

- **Who gets it**: everyone who will attend; on an event with role slots, the people in a slot. **Options** decides whether the **bench** gets it too (off by default).
- **It follows the sign-ups**: someone who withdraws or drops to the bench loses it; someone who moves up off the bench gets it.
- **When it comes off**: an hour after the event ends by default (**Options** changes it, 0 to 1440 minutes). The end is the start plus the event's length, or 2 hours if it has none. Cancelling the event takes it off too.
- **Nobody loses a role they already had**: someone who held the role before Alagos gave it keeps it. And if the same role is on two events, it stays until the last of them is over.

A role that carries a moderation or admin permission is never given, and Alagos needs **Manage Roles** with its own role above this one. Templates can carry the temporary role too (**Extras**), and each week of a repeating event gets it.

## Repeating events

On the **Schedule** tab, set **Recurrence** to **Weekly**, **Biweekly** (every two weeks) or **Every Other Day**. The event you are editing becomes the first of the series, and each later one is created automatically shortly before it is due (**Post before** on the Notifications tab, an hour by default) as its own post with a fresh sign-up list.

Good to know:

- A series always repeats from the date and time you set. **Recurrence Day** only changes how the post describes it ("Weekly on Thursday"); to move a series to another day, change its date.
- **Weekday time shift** moves the time on particular weekdays, for example `thu:-60` to start an hour earlier on Thursdays. Minutes, comma-separated.
- Series repeat on a fixed 24-hour clock, so after a daylight-saving change the time may shift by an hour. Edit the time if that matters.
- On the Free plan a server can have 3 repeating events at a time.

## Editing

`/event-list` shows your events (filter by Active, Cancelled, Completed or All); pick one to open the editor. On a posted event you can also press **✏️ Edit Event** under the post. Saving updates the live post.

On one week of a series, the post also has **📝 Edit Template**: that edits the series itself, so the change applies to every later week. Editing a single week changes only that week.

## Skipping a week

To call off one occurrence of a repeating event without ending the series, use `/event-skip`:

- `next` skips the next one (run it twice to skip two);
- `date` skips a particular date;
- `list` shows what is coming and what has been skipped;
- `undo` brings a skipped date back.

A skipped date gets no post, no reminder and no attendance. You can set a skip days ahead, before that week's post exists.

## Cancelling

**🚫 Cancel event** in the editor (it asks you to confirm), or `/event-cancel`. The post is marked cancelled and its sign-up buttons stop working; `/event-cancel` can delete the post instead. **Cancelling the first event of a series ends the whole series**: to call off one week, skip it.

Before an event is posted, the editor shows **🗑️ Delete event** instead. On an event you just created it deletes it; on one created earlier it only throws away your unsaved changes.

## After an event ends

By default an event's messages stay in the channel. To keep the channel tidy, open **🧹 After an event ends** on the **Channels** tab of `/guild-settings show` (needs **Manage settings**) and choose:

- **Leave them** (the default).
- **Remove Alagos's own posts**: the event post, its "has started!" message, its reminders and, in DC Dark Legion, its team post. Its thread is archived. Nobody else's messages are touched.
- **Clear the whole event channel**: every message in the **Event Post** channel older than the delay, **members' messages too**, except pinned ones. Alagos needs **Manage Messages** and **Read Message History** there, and you confirm by typing the channel's name (emojis, symbols and capitals can be left out: "raid signups" confirms "📅┃raid-signups"). Nothing is cleared from the oldest event that is still on: an event that has not ended, is inside the delay, or is waiting for its attendance keeps its post and every message after it, so members' talk about an upcoming event is never lost. Use it only for a channel where events are posted.

Then pick how long after the event ends: 1 hour, 6 hours, 1 day (the default), 3 days or a week. An event that records attendance waits for its attendance to be saved, for as long as you choose under **Wait for attendance to be saved**: don't wait, 1, 3 or 7 days (the default), never longer than your attendance edit window. After that its messages go even if attendance was never saved; it can still be recorded from **Record attendance** on the officer panel while the edit window allows. The first event of a repeating series is never touched.

Switching on only affects events that end from then on. **🧹 Tidy up past events** removes the messages of events that ended before. It also looks through Alagos's own older messages in the event and reminder channels ("has started!" messages, reminders and team posts from before Alagos kept track of them), matches each to its event, and removes those of events already tidied up. It reads only its own messages, never anyone else's. Saving a choice or tidying up starts removing at once; after that Alagos works through about 20 events every 10 minutes. The screen shows the last pass, the next, and what is still waiting and why (inside the delay, waiting for attendance, or no permission in a channel); press **🔄 Refresh** to follow it.

Nothing about the event is lost: its sign-ups and attendance stay in Alagos, and **📜 Past events** in the reports shows them.

## Banners

The banner is the picture at the top of an event's post. Every server has a set of **built-in banners**, free: Raid, PvP, PvE, Social, Training, Racing, Announcement and General. **An event with no banner chosen gets the one that fits its type**: a raid gets Raid, a scrim PvP, a practice Training, your own event types General.

Pick a banner in the editor's **Core Info** tab: **By event type** (the default), **No banner**, a built-in, or one of your own. Templates have the same choice under **Extras**.

**Your own banners** live in `/guild-settings show` → **Features & limits** → **🖼️ Banners**: **⬆️ Upload** an image (JPG, PNG, GIF or WEBP, up to 10 MB; wide 3:1 images look best) or **🔗 Add by link**. A link typed straight into the editor's banner field joins the library too. The free plan holds **3** of your own; Premium has no limit. Going back to Free never removes any: you just can't add more until you are under 3. Pick one of yours to rename or delete it; events that used a deleted banner go back to their type's banner.

`/event-banner-upload`, `/event-banner-list` and `/event-banner-set` still work and follow the same limit.
